timeline_events.summary: Al Gore begins his campaign to succeed Bill Clinton in the November 2000 presidential election, amid trailing polls and a challenge from Bill Bradley.
Al Gore formally announced his candidacy for the US presidency, promising moral leadership and distancing himself from Bill Clinton.
Al Gore moved his presidential campaign headquarters from Washington to Nashville as part of an effort to reinvent himself as an outsider in the race for the White House.
Al Gore and Bill Bradley held their first televised confrontation of the Democratic presidential campaign at Dartmouth College in New Hampshire.
US Friends of the Earth endorses Bill Bradley over Al Gore for the Democratic Party nomination, releasing a scorecard showing Bradley had a stronger environmental record than Gore.
Al Gore offers to halt all television and radio campaign ads and hold twice-weekly debates with Democratic presidential rival Bill Bradley, who dismisses the offer as a ploy.
Senator Edward Kennedy endorsed Al Gore for the Democratic presidential nomination, boosting his campaign ahead of the New Hampshire primary.
Al Gore was projected to win the Iowa Democratic caucuses with a 2:1 lead over Bill Bradley, according to a final poll.
Al Gore won the Iowa Democratic caucuses, defeating Bill Bradley by 63% to 35%.
Article discusses Al Gore’s presidential campaign, noting his qualifications and the political burden of his association with Bill Clinton.
Al Gore wins all Democratic Super Tuesday contests, including a runaway victory in New York, over Bill Bradley.
Al Gore and George W. Bush shifted into general election mode after decisive Super Tuesday primary victories, with Gore proposing twice-weekly televised debates and a mutual ban on TV advertising.
Al Gore clinched the Democratic nomination for the US presidential election after sweeping six southern state primaries, surpassing the required 2,168 delegates.
Al Gore and George W. Bush were close to clinching their party presidential nominations as six southern US states voted in primary contests.
John Prescott travels to Washington to meet Al Gore and Republican senators to support Gore's stance on global warming and the Kyoto agreement.

Supporters of Vice-President Al Gore are increasingly worried that he is losing the initiative in the 2000 US presidential election to Republican rival George W. Bush, who has re-established himself in the centre ground.
Al Gore turns to his wife, Tipper, to bolster his ailing US presidential campaign as an opinion poll shows him trailing Republican rival George W. Bush by 10 points.
Al Gore has assembled a glittering cast list of Hollywood endorsements, with 17 Oscar winners donating at least $1,000 each to his presidential campaign.
Al Gore plans to announce his Democratic vice-presidential running mate, aiming to recapture the initiative after the Republican convention.
Al Gore selects Senator Joseph Lieberman as his running mate, a move symbolically underlining the end of the Bill Clinton era.
US Vice-President and presidential candidate Al Gore announced Senator Joseph Lieberman as his running mate, making Lieberman the first Jewish candidate on a major party ticket.
Al Gore presents himself at the Democrat convention in Los Angeles for the Presidential race.
Al Gore arrives in Los Angeles to secure the Democratic Party's nomination and prepare for the presidential campaign with attack strategist Bob Shrum.
Al Gore accepts the Democratic presidential nomination in Los Angeles, declaring "I stand here tonight as my own man."

Al Gore surged into an opinion poll lead over George W. Bush following his performance at the Democratic convention, leading 48% to 42% among registered voters in a Newsweek poll and 47% to 46% among likely voters in a Gallup/CNN survey.
Article discusses Al Gore as the Democratic presidential candidate facing a potential third-party challenge from Ralph Nader.
George W. Bush's presidential campaign launches its first personal attack ad against Democratic rival Al Gore, mocking his character and credibility.
George W. Bush's campaign withdrew a television ad after Democrats claimed it included a subliminal message attacking Al Gore, with the word "rats" flashing before "bureaucrats."
Al Gore resists pressure to deploy Bill Clinton on the campaign trail in the final stretch of the presidential race.
Al Gore campaigned in Tennessee and Missouri, discussing education policy at Tennessee State University and holding rallies in Jackson and Kansas City.
Al Gore campaigns in his home state of Tennessee and other traditionally Democratic states as polls show a tight race with George W. Bush.
The article expresses hope that Al Gore wins the upcoming US presidential election, citing his flaws but arguing George Bush would be worse.

President Bill Clinton campaigned for Al Gore by urging black Americans to vote for the Democratic candidate, while the Gore camp said it intended to keep Clinton at arm's length in the main electoral battleground.

The article discusses Al Gore's character and campaign in the 2000 presidential election, noting that voters see him as dull and that his campaign is in trouble, while he tries to show a softer side before polling day.
Al Gore campaigns around the clock in the final days before the US presidential election, making a last push through battleground states.
A Harris Interactive poll indicates Al Gore could win the presidency in the electoral college despite George W. Bush leading the national popular vote.
George W. Bush visits Tennessee, Al Gore's home state, on the final day of the presidential campaign in an attempt to taunt his rival.
Al Gore is described as being neck and neck in the polls with rival George Bush in the presidential election.
Al Gore is projected to win the presidency with 281 electoral college votes leaning his way, while George W. Bush has 249, according to state-based polls ahead of the election.
Al Gore campaigns across several states on the final day before the election and is scheduled to cast his vote in Carthage, Tennessee.
Al Gore wins a slender but clear majority of the popular vote, though the final outcome of the Florida recount remains unclear.
Al Gore refuses to concede the disputed presidential election to George W. Bush, as his campaign mounts legal challenges over irregularities in Florida.
Al Gore's campaign chairman calls for hand recounts in four Florida counties, alleging serious irregularities with ballot layout.
Al Gore remains in a contested US presidential election with George W. Bush, as a Florida recount shows Bush leading by just 327 votes and overseas ballots remain uncounted.
Al Gore faces pressure from allies and opponents to accept the Florida recount result and not pursue legal challenges in the US presidential election.
Florida's Republican secretary of state ruled that all recounts must be completed and certified by the next day, dealing a setback to Al Gore's hopes of winning the US presidency.
Florida's top elections official announced that George W. Bush holds a 300-vote lead over Al Gore based on presidential vote returns submitted by all 67 counties.
Al Gore asked a Florida judge to force the state to count disputed presidential ballots being hand tallied after a deadline had passed.
Democrats were divided over how much further Al Gore should pursue his post-election struggle for the White House, as Republicans threatened to fight him to the electoral college and beyond.

Al Gore's campaign asks the Florida Supreme Court to order Miami-Dade officials to resume and complete a full hand recount or at least count the 10,000 undervotes, as the battle over Florida's electoral votes reaches the US Supreme Court.
Al Gore launched a legal, political, and public relations offensive to challenge George W. Bush's certified victory in Florida and keep his White House hopes alive.

A Florida state judge rejected Al Gore's challenge to the certified presidential election results, refusing recounts in Palm Beach and Miami-Dade counties and dealing a serious setback to Gore's hopes of preventing George W. Bush from winning.
Al Gore conceded the presidential race to George W. Bush after the US Supreme Court halted Florida recounts.
Al Gore announced plans to teach and write for the next few months while considering his political future.

A Miami Herald review of uncounted undervotes in Miami-Dade County suggests Al Gore would have gained only 49 net votes there, leaving George Bush ahead by 140 votes in Florida even if manual recounts had proceeded.

A Palm Beach Post survey of undervotes in Palm Beach county shows Al Gore would have gained 784 more votes than George Bush if every excluded paper with some kind of mark had been counted, enough to overtake Bush's 537-vote statewide margin in Florida.

A comprehensive study of disputed Florida ballot papers found that George Bush would probably still have won the disputed presidential election vote in Florida if the US Supreme Court had allowed a recount, though Al Gore probably would have won under new vote-counting rules.
Al Gore accused the Bush administration of incompetence in the hunt for Osama bin Laden and criticized its handling of the war on terrorism.

Al Gore is promoting two new books, "Joined at the Heart" and "The Spirit of Family," co-authored with his wife Tipper, as part of a carefully planned campaign amid speculation about whether he will run for president in 2004.
Al Gore announced he had decided against running for the presidency in 2004.
Al Gore is planning to launch a liberal cable TV news network to challenge the dominance of rightwing media such as Fox News.
Former US vice-president Al Gore is reportedly in talks to acquire the cable network Newsworld International from Vivendi Universal in a deal valued at $70m.
Al Gore is due to endorse Howard Dean in the Democratic presidential race at a rally in Harlem.
Laurie David saw Al Gore give a 10-minute version of his PowerPoint presentation on global warming and set the film An Inconvenient Truth in motion.

Al Gore and partner Joel Hyatt confirm the acquisition of cable channel News World International from Vivendi Universal, which they plan to transform into an independent network for 18- to 34-year-old viewers.
Al Gore opens the Democratic National Convention, handing on the Democratic baton to John Kerry.

Al Gore and former Goldman Sachs executive David Blood launch Generation, a London-based investment firm focused on long-term sustainability, which will begin managing their own money in the new year and seek clients toward the end of the first quarter of 2005.
Al Gore released the Oscar-winning documentary An Inconvenient Truth, which raised global comprehension of the causes and dangers of climate change.
The documentary "An Inconvenient Truth," featuring Al Gore's climate change presentations, receives standing ovations at the Sundance Film Festival.
Al Gore appears at the Sundance Film Festival in the documentary "An Inconvenient Truth," a film based on his multimedia presentation about global warming.

Al Gore gave a keynote speech at America's biggest media conference in Orlando, Florida, where he urged the media industry to contribute airtime to an upcoming public service campaign on global warming.
Al Gore's documentary about global warming, An Inconvenient Truth, is released in the US.
Al Gore is scheduled to speak at the Guardian Hay festival at 7 pm GMT.
Al Gore delivered a lecture at the Hay festival promoting his film An Inconvenient Truth and urging action on climate change, receiving a standing ovation.
Former US vice-president Al Gore met with UK Chancellor Gordon Brown in London to lobby on global warming and attended a private screening of his climate change documentary An Inconvenient Truth.
Al Gore's documentary An Inconvenient Truth is to be honoured with a Special Award from the Humanitas Prize organisation.
Al Gore said the internet could re-engage the electorate with politics on both sides of the Atlantic.
Al Gore is scheduled to deliver the Alternative MacTaggart Lecture at the MediaGuardian Edinburgh International Television Festival.
Former US vice president Al Gore's film on global warming, An Inconvenient Truth, is set to be shown in cinemas worldwide after receiving rave reviews in America and Europe.
An article discusses Al Gore's failure to win the 2000 US presidential election and argues that his strategy of distancing himself from Bill Clinton's achievements contributed to his defeat.
The documentary An Inconvenient Truth, narrated by Al Gore, opens in British cinemas.
Al Gore unveiled plans to launch a UK version of his user-generated network Current TV with the help of BSkyB.
Sky announced a deal to bring Al Gore's Current TV, a channel featuring viewer-created clips, to the UK and Ireland.
Al Gore, as a non-executive director of Apple, is on a committee investigating the company's backdating of share options granted between 1997 and 2002.
Al Gore announces that Current TV will launch on Virgin Media in mid-March, following a similar deal with Sky in October.
Al Gore announced the "Live Earth" concerts, a series of seven global concerts to raise awareness of climate change, scheduled for July 7, 2007.
Al Gore was among the announced nominees for the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize, nominated for his campaign to draw attention to global warming.
Al Gore and his film An Inconvenient Truth are expected to share the Academy Award.
Channel 4 wins the terrestrial television rights to Al Gore's Oscar-winning documentary An Inconvenient Truth, with the film set to air in 2008.
Al Gore unveils the British version of his Current TV network, a channel relying on viewer-created content.
Former US Vice-President Al Gore urged the pensions industry to adopt longer-term investment goals, warning that short-termism risks undermining sustainable economies and progress on climate change.
Al Gore returned to Congress to testify on global warming, receiving a positive reception.
Al Gore collected the best documentary Oscar for his film on global warming, An Inconvenient Truth.
Apple's independent directors, including Al Gore, publicly expressed complete confidence in Steve Jobs amid a stock options scandal.
Al Gore spoke at the Cannes advertising festival about the ad industry's role in tackling climate change and received the first-ever "green" Cannes Advertising Festival award.
A New Hampshire poll suggests Democratic voters would prefer former Vice-President Al Gore over declared 2008 contenders, though Gore has repeatedly denied planning a White House run.
A poll suggests Democratic voters would prefer former Vice President Al Gore to declared contenders including Hillary Clinton, though Gore has repeatedly denied planning a White House run.
Al Gore III, son of former US vice-president Al Gore, was arrested on suspicion of possessing marijuana and prescription drugs after being pulled over for speeding in California.
Al Gore's Current TV hires MTV Networks Europe's David Ridings as its first marketing director for the UK and Ireland operation.
Former US vice-president Al Gore is working on a new environmental book, The Path to Survival, a sequel to An Inconvenient Truth, planned for publication in spring 2008.

A high court judge ruled that Al Gore's documentary An Inconvenient Truth can still be shown in secondary schools but only if accompanied by fresh guidance notes to balance its "one-sided" views, after identifying nine scientific errors in the film.
Al Gore and the UN climate change panel share the 2007 Nobel peace prize for raising awareness of the risks of climate change.
Al Gore wins Nobel Peace Prize.
Al Gore and the UN climate change panel (IPCC) are announced as joint winners of the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize for raising awareness of the risks of climate change.

A High Court ruling required Al Gore's climate change documentary to be screened in secondary schools with guidance notes to balance its claims, following a challenge by a school governor supported by a network of business interests linked to fuel and mining lobbies.
Al Gore is rumoured to be considering a last-minute bid to be the Democratic party's presidential candidate.
Al Gore was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for alerting the world to the dangers of man-made climate change.
Al Gore said he had no plans to run for the White House despite winning the Nobel peace prize.
Al Gore rules out running as a candidate in the 2008 presidential elections, saying he has no plans to be a candidate again and is instead focused on a global campaign to address the climate crisis.
Al Gore's interactive television company Current Media plans to float on the Nasdaq stock market to pay off $36.5m in debts.
Al Gore emerges as a potential power broker and possible mediator in the Democratic nomination battle between Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama, while remaining neutral.
Apple shareholders approved a proposal for a regular vote on executive remuneration despite opposition from Steve Jobs and boardroom colleagues including Al Gore.
Al Gore unveils a $300 million advertising campaign intended to force a debate on climate change during the presidential elections.
Al Gore announced he would run again for president of the United States, and in November he won the White House in a landslide.
Al Gore launched a drive to mobilize 10 million volunteers through his Alliance for Climate Protection to pressure politicians to act on climate change.
Al Gore is spending $300 million on a three-year US advertising campaign aimed at prompting political action on climate change.
Al Gore endorses Barack Obama for president and vows to do whatever he can to ensure Obama is elected.
Former Vice President Al Gore asked the American people to join an ambitious plan to source 100% of American electricity from "clean and truly renewable" sources in 10 years.
ABC refuses to air an advert produced by Al Gore's environmental group, the Alliance for Climate Protection, ruling its content too controversial for television.
Al Gore urges the US to set a goal of moving to 100% renewable energy within 10 years, calling on Barack Obama to make it one of his first acts as president.
Al Gore calls for a tougher global carbon dioxide limit of 350 parts per million at UN climate talks in Poznan, Poland.

Al Gore testified before the Senate foreign relations committee, urging swift passage of Barack Obama's economic stimulus plan with its green provisions and calling for action toward an international climate treaty in Copenhagen.
Al Gore says in a newspaper interview that a political tipping point has been reached and he believes a global climate deal will be agreed at the UN climate talks in Copenhagen in December.
An opinion article criticizes Al Gore's film "An Inconvenient Truth" for exaggerating climate change dangers and frightening children.
Current TV, backed by Al Gore, has shifted from user-submitted social video toward social networking and thematically programmed shows, including WebMash and Upstream.
Al Gore publishes his sequel to An Inconvenient Truth, titled Our Choice: A Plan to Solve the Climate Crisis.
Al Gore's new book launch prompts questions about whether his investments in green technology amount to a conflict of interest.

Al Gore called on activists to press President Obama and the US Senate to set an April 22 deadline for passing climate change legislation and urged the international community to sign a fully fledged climate treaty by July 2010.
Mark Watson brings Al Gore's climate-change lecture, adapted into a comedy show, to London during the week of the Copenhagen conference.
Former US Vice-President Al Gore and his wife Tipper announced they are separating after 40 years of marriage.
Al Gore's Generation Investment Management is set to roughly double its money on its 1% stake in Ocado as the online grocery retailer prepares to float.
Al Gore's book "Our Choice" was released as an interactive iPad app developed by Push Pop Press.
An app based on former US vice president Al Gore's latest climate change book, Our Choice, is released by Push Pop Press in partnership with Gore and his publisher Rodale.

Al Gore publishes a Rolling Stone article arguing the climate crisis is a struggle for the soul of America and criticizing the US electoral system and President Obama's failure to make the case for climate action.
Al Gore returns with a new climate campaign, the Climate Reality project, which is set to kick off with a 24-hour live streamed event on 14 September.

Facebook acquires Push Pop Press, the startup behind Al Gore's Our Choice book-app, with Push Pop Press' share of the app's profits to be donated to Gore's environmental campaigning group The Climate Reality Project.
Al Gore will launch the Climate Reality Project's "24 Hours of Reality" campaign, a worldwide multimedia event to broadcast the reality of the climate crisis.
Apple board member Al Gore said at a speaking event in South Africa that new iPhones are coming out next month.
Al Gore's Alliance for Climate Protection dropped its bid to control the .eco internet domain, leaving the way open for a rival bid supported by Mikhail Gorbachev.
Al Gore warned that there is now clear proof that climate change is directly responsible for extreme and devastating floods, storms and droughts that displaced millions of people this year.

Al Gore claimed that scientists have clear proof climate change is directly responsible for extreme weather events that displaced millions of people in 2011, a claim criticized by scientist Myles Allen as overplaying the link between climate change and weather.
BSkyB axes Al Gore's Current TV from its pay-TV lineup, threatening the channel's UK closure.

Al Gore and David Blood, founders of Generation Investment Management, published a white paper calling for reforms to capitalism, including ending quarterly earnings guidance, to promote long-term and environmentally sustainable investing.
Al Gore calls on Barack Obama to act boldly on climate change and urges him to push for a carbon tax during fiscal cliff negotiations.
Al Gore launches the second annual 24 Hours of Reality event focused on connecting extreme weather to the climate crisis.
Al-Jazeera agreed to buy Current TV, the cable network co-founded by former US vice-president Al Gore, in a deal reported to be worth $500m.
Al-Jazeera buys Current TV, the cable channel co-founded by Al Gore, giving the network a chance to expand in the US market.
Keith Olbermann settles a $50m lawsuit against Al Gore's Current TV in mediation, avoiding a scheduled trial.
Al Gore says extreme weather events are a "gamechanger" for public awareness of climate change, speaking at the World Economic Forum in Davos.
Producers of An Inconvenient Truth discuss a potential sequel to the Al Gore climate change documentary.
Pharrell Williams and Al Gore announce a second round of Live Earth concerts, planned for 18 June 2015 across all seven continents to promote awareness of climate change.
Former US vice-president Al Gore's business partner David Blood warns investors of fossil fuel risks, challenging fund managers to adopt radical new approaches to fossil fuel investments.
Al Gore criticizes Barack Obama for allowing Arctic drilling, calling it "insane" and urging a ban on oil and gas activity in the polar region.
Al Gore called on the British government to resume its former leadership on climate change and criticized its rollback of support for renewable energy.
Al Gore’s planned global Live Earth concerts are downgraded to a Paris webcast event on 13–14 November that is closed to the public and streamed online.
Al Gore met with President-elect Donald Trump and his daughter Ivanka at Trump Tower in New York City, describing the session as a lengthy and productive search for common ground on climate change.
A follow-up to An Inconvenient Truth, featuring Al Gore, was confirmed to be among the opening night films at the forthcoming Sundance film festival.
Al Gore’s documentary An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power is scheduled to open the Sundance film festival.
A review is published of "An Inconvenient Sequel," a documentary following Al Gore's climate change advocacy and his preparations for the 2015 UN Climate Change Conference in Paris.
Al Gore’s Climate Reality Project held a three-day “Climate Reality Leaders” training in Denver, Colorado, with 972 attendees from 42 countries.

Al Gore said the fight against climate change is one of humanity’s great moral movements, alongside the abolition of slavery, the defeat of apartheid, votes for women and gay rights, and said the battle can be won despite the recent US withdrawal from the Paris climate accord.
A review is published of "An Inconvenient Sequel," a documentary following Al Gore through 2015 and 2016 as he addresses climate change and the Climate Reality Leadership Corps program.
A review is published of "An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power," a documentary featuring Al Gore's climate change advocacy.
Al Gore’s recent appearance on Capitol Hill marked his dominance in Washington’s debate about the science of global warming.

facts.text: On 1999-12-01, US Friends of the Earth endorsed Bill Bradley over Al Gore for the Democratic nomination, releasing a scorecard showing Bradley had a stronger environmental record.
On 2000-01-25, Al Gore won the Iowa Democratic caucuses, defeating Bill Bradley by 63% to 35%.
On 2000-03-14, Al Gore clinched the Democratic nomination after sweeping six southern state primaries, surpassing the required 2,168 delegates.
On 2000-08-07, Al Gore selected Senator Joseph Lieberman as his running mate, symbolically underlining the end of the Bill Clinton era.
On 2000-08-17, Al Gore accepted the Democratic presidential nomination in Los Angeles, declaring "I stand here tonight as my own man."
On 2000-11-03, with the 2000 election approaching, Al Gore was seen by voters as dull and his campaign was in trouble, while he tried to show a softer side before polling day.
On 2000-12-13, Al Gore conceded the presidential race to George W. Bush after the US Supreme Court halted Florida recounts.
On 2007-10-12, Al Gore and the UN climate change panel (IPCC) were announced as joint winners of the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize for raising awareness of the risks of climate change.

event-5091d347e4c01737.summary: Former US vice president Al Gore's film on global warming, An Inconvenient Truth, is set to be shown in cinemas worldwide after receiving rave reviews in America and Europe.

event-2b51a7f54b1b4bd3.summary: An article discusses Al Gore's failure to win the 2000 US presidential election and argues that his strategy of distancing himself from Bill Clinton's achievements contributed to his defeat.

event-56c3f1aec706838b.summary: The documentary An Inconvenient Truth, narrated by Al Gore, opens in British cinemas.

event-638845fad5f397d0.summary: Al Gore unveiled plans to launch a UK version of his user-generated network Current TV with the help of BSkyB.

event-0fdc792c0626a3b4.summary: Sky announced a deal to bring Al Gore's Current TV, a channel featuring viewer-created clips, to the UK and Ireland.

event-2cee0a2ce63a7afb.summary: Al Gore, as a non-executive director of Apple, is on a committee investigating the company's backdating of share options granted between 1997 and 2002.

event-7eda698362cca2e1.summary: Al Gore announces that Current TV will launch on Virgin Media in mid-March, following a similar deal with Sky in October.

event-3b1ae1ceef6e2c5f.summary: Al Gore announced the "Live Earth" concerts, a series of seven global concerts to raise awareness of climate change, scheduled for July 7, 2007.

event-0eae401ba690e083.summary: Al Gore was among the announced nominees for the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize, nominated for his campaign to draw attention to global warming.

event-88b22675343ba87c.summary: Al Gore and his film An Inconvenient Truth are expected to share the Academy Award.

event-98e568ee184ebfa9.summary: Channel 4 wins the terrestrial television rights to Al Gore's Oscar-winning documentary An Inconvenient Truth, with the film set to air in 2008.

event-443e09b3e9411c44.summary: Al Gore unveils the British version of his Current TV network, a channel relying on viewer-created content.

event-8c2208022171f2c6.summary: Former US Vice-President Al Gore urged the pensions industry to adopt longer-term investment goals, warning that short-termism risks undermining sustainable economies and progress on climate change.

event-c9d7b7500922694d.summary: Al Gore returned to Congress to testify on global warming, receiving a positive reception.

event-5c2b7025c2b4c39f.summary: Al Gore collected the best documentary Oscar for his film on global warming, An Inconvenient Truth.

event-e27b9dad94747e07.summary: Apple's independent directors, including Al Gore, publicly expressed complete confidence in Steve Jobs amid a stock options scandal.

event-664f99628c6fbf67.summary: Al Gore spoke at the Cannes advertising festival about the ad industry's role in tackling climate change and received the first-ever "green" Cannes Advertising Festival award.

event-f65642559deb9c32.summary: A New Hampshire poll suggests Democratic voters would prefer former Vice-President Al Gore over declared 2008 contenders, though Gore has repeatedly denied planning a White House run.

event-2a87d7416fc6a119.summary: A poll suggests Democratic voters would prefer former Vice President Al Gore to declared contenders including Hillary Clinton, though Gore has repeatedly denied planning a White House run.

event-9d75c0e905437a3f.summary: Al Gore III, son of former US vice-president Al Gore, was arrested on suspicion of possessing marijuana and prescription drugs after being pulled over for speeding in California.

event-57aefb297097efca.summary: Al Gore's Current TV hires MTV Networks Europe's David Ridings as its first marketing director for the UK and Ireland operation.

event-8ebfae9299a9492c.summary: Former US vice-president Al Gore is working on a new environmental book, The Path to Survival, a sequel to An Inconvenient Truth, planned for publication in spring 2008.

event-44e271d76e3b92ef.summary: A high court judge ruled that Al Gore's documentary An Inconvenient Truth can still be shown in secondary schools but only if accompanied by fresh guidance notes to balance its "one-sided" views, after identifying nine scientific errors in the film.

event-51be803d0d4d7b08.summary: Al Gore and the UN climate change panel share the 2007 Nobel peace prize for raising awareness of the risks of climate change.

event-6ce3ab412487ae9a.summary: Al Gore wins Nobel Peace Prize.

event-9649cb12a03b01a9.summary: Al Gore and the UN climate change panel (IPCC) are announced as joint winners of the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize for raising awareness of the risks of climate change.

event-4fe533b704cf4247.summary: A High Court ruling required Al Gore's climate change documentary to be screened in secondary schools with guidance notes to balance its claims, following a challenge by a school governor supported by a network of business interests linked to fuel and mining lobbies.

event-68d189f4b8ae1028.summary: Al Gore is rumoured to be considering a last-minute bid to be the Democratic party's presidential candidate.

event-7cd286bac10a0cfb.summary: Al Gore was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for alerting the world to the dangers of man-made climate change.

event-d9c57fca988e938f.summary: Al Gore said he had no plans to run for the White House despite winning the Nobel peace prize.

event-a7df7cf6b839fb04.summary: Al Gore rules out running as a candidate in the 2008 presidential elections, saying he has no plans to be a candidate again and is instead focused on a global campaign to address the climate crisis.

event-279852b7d1ed05a1.summary: Al Gore's interactive television company Current Media plans to float on the Nasdaq stock market to pay off $36.5m in debts.

event-3bca4bb88c3d1da8.summary: Al Gore emerges as a potential power broker and possible mediator in the Democratic nomination battle between Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama, while remaining neutral.

event-431babe13bf24682.summary: Apple shareholders approved a proposal for a regular vote on executive remuneration despite opposition from Steve Jobs and boardroom colleagues including Al Gore.

event-f19ac84351e30f07.summary: Al Gore unveils a $300 million advertising campaign intended to force a debate on climate change during the presidential elections.

event-56ef0ced1fe39b90.summary: Al Gore announced he would run again for president of the United States, and in November he won the White House in a landslide.

event-f46a25afe0c2a2ca.summary: Al Gore launched a drive to mobilize 10 million volunteers through his Alliance for Climate Protection to pressure politicians to act on climate change.

event-27a181eae9899451.summary: Al Gore is spending $300 million on a three-year US advertising campaign aimed at prompting political action on climate change.

event-1874de93604e0709.summary: Al Gore endorses Barack Obama for president and vows to do whatever he can to ensure Obama is elected.

event-15a3cf8778cbcaa6.summary: Former Vice President Al Gore asked the American people to join an ambitious plan to source 100% of American electricity from "clean and truly renewable" sources in 10 years.

event-77edf446701df0c5.summary: ABC refuses to air an advert produced by Al Gore's environmental group, the Alliance for Climate Protection, ruling its content too controversial for television.

event-0cf63cf4d3ade3c5.summary: Al Gore urges the US to set a goal of moving to 100% renewable energy within 10 years, calling on Barack Obama to make it one of his first acts as president.

event-7b1a6493e4b198e3.summary: Al Gore calls for a tougher global carbon dioxide limit of 350 parts per million at UN climate talks in Poznan, Poland.

event-fd25b849c5ea3a48.summary: Al Gore testified before the Senate foreign relations committee, urging swift passage of Barack Obama's economic stimulus plan with its green provisions and calling for action toward an international climate treaty in Copenhagen.

event-19bb9d2f2352a3de.summary: Al Gore says in a newspaper interview that a political tipping point has been reached and he believes a global climate deal will be agreed at the UN climate talks in Copenhagen in December.

event-0cd463ce2eb7af67.summary: An opinion article criticizes Al Gore's film "An Inconvenient Truth" for exaggerating climate change dangers and frightening children.

event-4043fe848f62a468.summary: Current TV, backed by Al Gore, has shifted from user-submitted social video toward social networking and thematically programmed shows, including WebMash and Upstream.

event-2ee4a9a1e18d32d7.summary: Al Gore publishes his sequel to An Inconvenient Truth, titled Our Choice: A Plan to Solve the Climate Crisis.

event-4b8bdb7e586a4ec7.summary: Al Gore's new book launch prompts questions about whether his investments in green technology amount to a conflict of interest.

event-9251c1b90a619dda.summary: Al Gore called on activists to press President Obama and the US Senate to set an April 22 deadline for passing climate change legislation and urged the international community to sign a fully fledged climate treaty by July 2010.

event-3d5d14c137df6a3b.summary: Mark Watson brings Al Gore's climate-change lecture, adapted into a comedy show, to London during the week of the Copenhagen conference.

event-8ef791498405a29a.summary: Former US Vice-President Al Gore and his wife Tipper announced they are separating after 40 years of marriage.

event-7ed56f69d970fd4f.summary: Al Gore's Generation Investment Management is set to roughly double its money on its 1% stake in Ocado as the online grocery retailer prepares to float.

event-3072e3ee0c6842f0.summary: Al Gore's book "Our Choice" was released as an interactive iPad app developed by Push Pop Press.

event-a178374974350da3.summary: An app based on former US vice president Al Gore's latest climate change book, Our Choice, is released by Push Pop Press in partnership with Gore and his publisher Rodale.

event-0ba96eb11651e6b4.summary: Al Gore publishes a Rolling Stone article arguing the climate crisis is a struggle for the soul of America and criticizing the US electoral system and President Obama's failure to make the case for climate action.

event-ebefba6397fea9fb.summary: Al Gore returns with a new climate campaign, the Climate Reality project, which is set to kick off with a 24-hour live streamed event on 14 September.

event-3161e7585442279a.summary: Facebook acquires Push Pop Press, the startup behind Al Gore's Our Choice book-app, with Push Pop Press' share of the app's profits to be donated to Gore's environmental campaigning group The Climate Reality Project.

event-7448bf89276f4c05.summary: Al Gore will launch the Climate Reality Project's "24 Hours of Reality" campaign, a worldwide multimedia event to broadcast the reality of the climate crisis.

event-98f6006e4f3c5ca0.summary: Apple board member Al Gore said at a speaking event in South Africa that new iPhones are coming out next month.

event-541bc304dc8a5860.summary: Al Gore's Alliance for Climate Protection dropped its bid to control the .eco internet domain, leaving the way open for a rival bid supported by Mikhail Gorbachev.

event-b6170c39553d7347.summary: Al Gore warned that there is now clear proof that climate change is directly responsible for extreme and devastating floods, storms and droughts that displaced millions of people this year.

event-0bea8bc33e85475a.summary: Al Gore claimed that scientists have clear proof climate change is directly responsible for extreme weather events that displaced millions of people in 2011, a claim criticized by scientist Myles Allen as overplaying the link between climate change and weather.

event-2a4e3edfc894046c.summary: BSkyB axes Al Gore's Current TV from its pay-TV lineup, threatening the channel's UK closure.

event-1fc6ed6550332a40.summary: Al Gore and David Blood, founders of Generation Investment Management, published a white paper calling for reforms to capitalism, including ending quarterly earnings guidance, to promote long-term and environmentally sustainable investing.

event-7207ef5d31aa9ff8.summary: Al Gore calls on Barack Obama to act boldly on climate change and urges him to push for a carbon tax during fiscal cliff negotiations.

event-3a1426e6e5b28afd.summary: Al Gore launches the second annual 24 Hours of Reality event focused on connecting extreme weather to the climate crisis.

event-82720d3d841c8453.summary: Al-Jazeera agreed to buy Current TV, the cable network co-founded by former US vice-president Al Gore, in a deal reported to be worth $500m.

event-3efed7c1d432d25c.summary: Al-Jazeera buys Current TV, the cable channel co-founded by Al Gore, giving the network a chance to expand in the US market.

event-2146c6aef6a15783.summary: Keith Olbermann settles a $50m lawsuit against Al Gore's Current TV in mediation, avoiding a scheduled trial.

event-2af2b5df8a7402d7.summary: Al Gore says extreme weather events are a "gamechanger" for public awareness of climate change, speaking at the World Economic Forum in Davos.

event-ec86d6ad13d30b6c.summary: Producers of An Inconvenient Truth discuss a potential sequel to the Al Gore climate change documentary.

event-cd4beabc4368e1db.summary: Pharrell Williams and Al Gore announce a second round of Live Earth concerts, planned for 18 June 2015 across all seven continents to promote awareness of climate change.

event-6704371ef4672525.summary: Former US vice-president Al Gore's business partner David Blood warns investors of fossil fuel risks, challenging fund managers to adopt radical new approaches to fossil fuel investments.

event-a8d5c8340464549a.summary: Al Gore criticizes Barack Obama for allowing Arctic drilling, calling it "insane" and urging a ban on oil and gas activity in the polar region.

event-4b0ac95f77d04fe7.summary: Al Gore called on the British government to resume its former leadership on climate change and criticized its rollback of support for renewable energy.

event-b4ad155e414495a8.summary: Al Gore’s planned global Live Earth concerts are downgraded to a Paris webcast event on 13–14 November that is closed to the public and streamed online.

event-68f9f6f36ea4afba.summary: Al Gore met with President-elect Donald Trump and his daughter Ivanka at Trump Tower in New York City, describing the session as a lengthy and productive search for common ground on climate change.

event-efc826fa001743db.summary: A follow-up to An Inconvenient Truth, featuring Al Gore, was confirmed to be among the opening night films at the forthcoming Sundance film festival.

event-163f6994fd434a48.summary: Al Gore’s documentary An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power is scheduled to open the Sundance film festival.

event-b11e1bb84ce0aa63.summary: A review is published of "An Inconvenient Sequel," a documentary following Al Gore's climate change advocacy and his preparations for the 2015 UN Climate Change Conference in Paris.

event-52f4669954f0197e.summary: Al Gore’s Climate Reality Project held a three-day “Climate Reality Leaders” training in Denver, Colorado, with 972 attendees from 42 countries.

event-0f17292a8a2d8261.summary: Al Gore said the fight against climate change is one of humanity’s great moral movements, alongside the abolition of slavery, the defeat of apartheid, votes for women and gay rights, and said the battle can be won despite the recent US withdrawal from the Paris climate accord.

event-f2c5516c6912cce1.summary: A review is published of "An Inconvenient Sequel," a documentary following Al Gore through 2015 and 2016 as he addresses climate change and the Climate Reality Leadership Corps program.

event-001c51b87d217793.summary: A review is published of "An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power," a documentary featuring Al Gore's climate change advocacy.

event-a55542d5b0d66b52.summary: Al Gore’s recent appearance on Capitol Hill marked his dominance in Washington’s debate about the science of global warming.
